They were red in the face, they got so warm, And rested, breathless, arm in arm. Yoo-hoo! Yoo-ho! And a hey-nonny-no! Breast on breast soft lying! “Keep your hands to yourself,” said she, “T know how girls, young brides-to-be, Are stood up by no-goods like you!” But soon hed coaxed her to the side, And the music rang out far and wide: Yoo-hoo! Yoo-ho! And a hey-nonny-no! And the fiddler, he played too!

@@U00244@@
How good it is of you, Doctor, not to scorn our holiday, but come to mingle with us folk, scholar that we know you are. Take this, now, this jug, this handsome jug, filled at the tap with our freshest brew. I give it to you with our wish that it not only quench your thirst, but every drop that it contains should lengthen your life by another day.

@@U00246@@
Thank you, old man, and health and happiness to you.

@@U00247@@
(The people gather round him.)

@@U00249@@
It’s kind of you, truly kind, to visit us on this happy day. In years gone by, in very dark times,

他们脸色通红，变得如此温暖， 臂挽臂，气喘吁吁地休息。哟吼！哟呵！还有一个嘿-老妈-不！乳房对乳房柔软的躺着！ “管好你的手，”她说，“我不知道女孩们，年轻的准新娘，是如何被像你这样的废物所欺骗的！”但很快他就把她哄到了一边，音乐声远远地响起：哟呼！哟呵！还有一个嘿-老妈-不！还有小提琴手，他也演奏！

@@U00244@@
医生，您不蔑视我们的假期，而是来与我们这些民间人士、学者打成一片，我们知道您是这样的人，您真是太好了。拿着这个，现在，这个罐子，这个漂亮的罐子，在水龙头上装满了我们最新鲜的啤酒。我把它送给你，希望它不仅能解你的渴，而且它所含的每一滴水都能让你的生命延长一天。

@@U00246@@
谢谢您，老人家，祝您健康快乐。

@@U00247@@
（人们聚集在他周围。）

@@U00249@@
